text:
Maya R.: Hi team—my start date is 4/01. Two quick things: my offer mentioned a $5k relocation payment and a monthly commuter stipend. 1) Will the relocation be split or paid in one lump? 2) I plan to start the week of a company holiday(office closed Thurs). Will the commuter prepay card activate before that? 3) I need to enroll my domestic partner on medical; what proofs are acceptable?

Jordan (People Ops): Welcome, Maya! For most offers we do a single lump relocation payment on the first payroll after your status is active, but exceptions exist. If you'd rather split it across two runs we can check the offer approval. Holiday weeks can delay physical card activation since shipping and payroll flags depend on the HR activation date. Can you confirm if you selected physical card or virtual EFT in the stipend form?

Maya R.: I selected "virtual card" in the form. Also would prefer the relocation split if possible because of moving deposits.

Evan (Payroll): Virtual card usually activates faster (once we flip your status to active), but activation may still be blocked until your direct deposit and I-9 are processed. If you upload docs by EOD Tue we can probably get the virtual commuter card live before the holiday. Regarding the $5k, payroll treats relocation payments as supplemental wages; we can do a one-time gross payment or split it into two payrolls. If you DM me the offer ID I can flag it for split and confirm tax withholding impacts.

Priya (Benefits): For domestic partner enrollment we accept: signed DP affidavit + one of: recent joint lease, joint bank statement, or utility bill with both names dated within 60 days. If you don't have joint docs yet, we can accept a notarized affidavit plus a secondary supporting document (e.g., shared insurance policy). Enroll via the benefits portal within 30 days of start.

Maya R.: Thanks! I can upload the bank statement tonight. One more: if the relocation is split, does that change tax withholding or benefits eligibility date?

Evan (Payroll): Splitting the payment does not change your benefits eligibility date. It only affects how the supplemental income is taxed across payroll runs. We'll show line items like "Relocation" on each run. Net difference is mostly timing of withholding; if you need projected net amounts I can run an estimate for your state (please DM state + exemptions).

Jordan (People Ops): Action items: 1) Maya to upload bank stmt + completed I-9 by Tue. 2) Maya to DM Evan with offer ID + state. 3) Priya will watch benefits portal for DP docs. I'll follow up if we need approval to split relocation.

onboarding-bot: Reminder: New hire docs due within 3 business days. Benefits enrollment window: 30 days from start.

Maya R.: Got it, thanks everyone! I'll upload tonight and DM Evan. Appreciate the quick responses :pray:
